bug_description.normalized: The staged witness for OVS's `ofctl_parse_target` is the exact 3-byte buffer `0x63 0x20 0x00`. The harness maps byte 0 to `command = OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT` and passes bytes 1..2 as the single-space C string `" "` into `ofctl_parse_flow`. `parse_ofp_flow_mod_str` accepts that blank delete-strict flow, leaves `usable_protocols` at `OFPUTIL_P_ANY`, and materializes a heap-backed `fm.match`. `ofctl_parse_flows__` then takes the usable-protocol path and destroys `fm->match`, but `ofctl_parse_flow` still unconditionally calls `minimatch_destroy(&fm.match)` after the callee returns. The same miniflow allocation is therefore freed twice, and AddressSanitizer reports the second destroy at `ofctl_parse_flow:65`. The fix removes the caller-side destroy and centralizes cleanup inside `ofctl_parse_flows__`.

source.code: error = parse_ofp_flow_mod_str(&fm, input, NULL, NULL, command, &usable_protocols);
source.description: First project statement after the libFuzzer boundary that consumes the attacker-controlled flow string and command to build the flow-mod object `fm` and the `usable_protocols` state that decides whether the callee cleanup runs.
source.value_from: The staged PoC file is exactly three bytes: `0x63 0x20 0x00`. After the harness checks accept it, line 103 computes `command = (0x63 % OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT) + 1 = 4`, i.e. `OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT`, and line 106 passes bytes 1..2 as the one-space C string `" "` into `ofctl_parse_flow`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Successful parsing materializes the caller-owned `fm.match` object. Inside `minimatch_init`, OVS allocates the heap-backed miniflow storage that is later freed once in `ofctl_parse_flows__` and a second time in `ofctl_parse_flow`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `ofctl_parse_flow` destroys `fm.match` after returning from `ofctl_parse_flows__`, even though that callee has already destroyed the same heap-backed match object on the successful usable-protocol path.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports the crashing free in `minimatch_destroy` with the application frame at `ofctl_parse_flow` line 65; the previous free comes from the line-64 call into `ofctl_parse_flows__`.

root_cause.description: Duplicate ownership cleanup in the caller. `ofctl_parse_flow` still assumes it must destroy `fm.match` after calling `ofctl_parse_flows__`, but the callee already destroys `fm->match` on the successful `usable_protocols & OFPUTIL_P_ANY` path.
root_cause.note: The fixing commit deletes this line and changes the `no usable protocol` early return in `ofctl_parse_flows__` into `goto free`, so both `ofpacts` and `match` are cleaned exactly once in the callee.

coarse_trace.summary: The 3-byte witness passes the harness guards, maps byte 0 to `command = OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT`, and passes the single-space tail string into `ofctl_parse_flow`.
`parse_ofp_flow_mod_str` successfully parses the blank delete-strict flow, leaves `usable_protocols` nonzero, and materializes the heap-backed `fm.match` object.
Because `usable_protocols & OFPUTIL_P_ANY` is true, the callee destroys `fm->match`; control then returns to `ofctl_parse_flow`, which destroys the same match again and triggers the ASan double-free.

fine_trace.note: The staged PoC bytes are exactly `0x63 0x20 0x00`. The harness checks at lines 90-91 accept this buffer because `size == 3`, the last byte is NUL, and the tail string contains no newline. Line 103 computes `command = 4` because `OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT == 4`, and line 106 sets `input` to the one-space C string `" "`; this call passes that exact command/string pair into the project parser helper.

fine_trace.code: error = parse_ofp_flow_mod_str(&fm, input, NULL, NULL, command, &usable_protocols);
fine_trace.note: This is the first project statement after the libFuzzer boundary that consumes the attacker-controlled flow text. With `command = OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT` and `input = " "`, `parse_ofp_str__` starts `*usable_protocols` at `OFPUTIL_P_ANY` (lib/ofp-flow.c:1495), sets `fields = F_OUT_PORT | F_PRIORITY` for delete-strict (1533-1534), sees no key/value pairs in the whitespace-only string, and returns success (`error == NULL`). The successful parse leaves `usable_protocols` nonzero and makes `fm.match` eligible for later cleanup.

On the same success path, `parse_ofp_str__` materializes the catch-all `match` into caller-owned `fm.match`. `minimatch_init` allocates the underlying miniflow storage via `miniflow_alloc` at `lib/match.c:1737` (the allocation context named by ASan) and stores that heap pointer in the `fm.match` object later referenced by both destroy sites.

The early-return guard is false for this witness because step 2 left `usable_protocols` at `OFPUTIL_P_ANY`. `ofctl_parse_flows__` therefore does not return at line 25 and instead continues into the loop that encodes the flow and frees the parsed `fm` resources.

Inside the successful usable-protocol path, `ofctl_parse_flows__` destroys the same `fm.match` object created in step 3. After this call, the heap region that ASan identifies as `[0x603000000040, 0x603000000060)` has been freed once, but the caller-owned `fm.match` still carries the stale pointer when control returns to `ofctl_parse_flow`.

Root cause and sink. After step 5 returns, `ofctl_parse_flow` still unconditionally destroys `fm.match` again. `minimatch_destroy` therefore calls `free(match->flow)` on the already-freed allocation a second time, matching the ASan crash stack at `ofctl_parse_flow:65` and the previous-free stack that comes through the line-64 call into `ofctl_parse_flows__`. The patch removes this caller-side destroy and centralizes cleanup in `ofctl_parse_flows__`.

allocation_context.note: ASan attributes the double-freed allocation to `miniflow_alloc` inside `minimatch_init`; that allocation is the heap-backed storage later owned by `fm.match`.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack reports the line-64 call site in `ofctl_parse_flow` because the first destroy happens through that call into `ofctl_parse_flows__`; the actual source-level first free is line 45 here.

format.name: 3-byte `ofctl_parse_target` witness buffer
format.contract: Exactly the staged 3-byte input `0x63 0x20 0x00` observed in `gt_results/arvo_11408/poc`: byte 0 selects `command = OFPFC_DELETE_STRICT`, byte 1 is a single-space flow string, and byte 2 is the required NUL terminator. This exact buffer makes `parse_ofp_flow_mod_str` return success with nonzero `usable_protocols` and a materialized `fm.match`, so `ofctl_parse_flows__` destroys that match once and `ofctl_parse_flow` destroys it a second time.
